rv.q: But the biggest limitation here is that the story simply doesn’t have a satisfying ending and, although it raises smart thematic questions, “Highway Patrol” lags as it brings it all to a point.
Watching Delany’s story unfold made for a marvelous night of theatre.
Dana Delaney is absolutely outstanding in this production, as is the entire cast. I highly recommend this funny, touching, yet haunting, modern play.
The real question, the one that Delany and her collaborators use to craft a highly suspenseful, hugely entertaining evening at the theater, is: why?

Mike Donahue's strong directorial hand—he is one of the four creators of the play along with Silverman, Delany, and Dane Laffrey—moves the play along and allows us to make sense of its twists and turns.
I was thoroughly intrigued with the storyline of Highway Patrol, and I recommend you get your tickets to this fantastic play.
Bold, daring and original, it’s a show worth seeing.
The premise for HIGHWAY PATROL is fascinating.
The "Highway Patrol" story probably belongs in a venue other than live theater—a place for big emotions and gestures, which this material lacks.
If you love good theater? This one is for you!
Highway Patrol does an excellent job of demonstrating disaffection, but it fails to engage our affection.

cn.t: Critics find this true story of Dana Delany's catfishing experience timely and engaging, praising her vulnerable performance, though some feel the material doesn't quite sustain a full play.
